question: Aryabhatta is believed to be one of the greatest astronomers of the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aryabhatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aryabhatta was a prominent Indian mathematician and astronomer who lived during the Gupta period, around 476-550 CE.
 
• He is best known for his work "Aryabhatiya," which covers arithmetic, algebra, plane trigonometry, and spherical trigonometry, along with continued fractions, quadratic equations, sums of power series, and a table of sines.
 
• Aryabhatta's astronomical calculations included the Earth's circumference and the theory that the Earth rotates on its axis, thus explaining the apparent westward motion of stars.
 
• His calculations of the solar and lunar eclipses were remarkably accurate for his time.
 
• The Aryabhata satellite, India’s first satellite, was named in his honor and launched in 1975.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Period:**

 
 
• The Gupta period is often referred to as the Golden Age of India due to significant achievements in arts, science, and literature.
 
• The period saw the flourishing of Sanskrit literature and the creation of important works like the plays of Kalidasa.
 
• In addition to Aryabhatta, other notable scholars from this period include Varahamihira and Brahmagupta.
 
• Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II were some of the prominent rulers of the Gupta dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Contributions:**
 
 
• Aryabhatta's approximation of pi (π) was highly accurate, calculated as 3.1416.
 
• He introduced the concept of zero as a placeholder and the decimal system in Indian mathematics.
 
• Aryabhatta's work on the sidereal periods of the planets was crucial for the development of Indian astronomy.
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Achievements:**
 
 
• Aryabhatta's work laid the foundation for the development of trigonometry in India.
 
• He provided solutions to quadratic equations and worked on the summation of series.
 
• His work influenced later mathematicians in India and the Islamic world.
 
 
 
• **Aryabhatiya:**
 
 
• The text is divided into four sections: Gitikapada, Ganitapada, Kalakriyapada, and Golapada.
 
• It covers a wide range of mathematical and astronomical topics, including time calculations, planetary positions, and eclipses.
 
• The work was highly influential and was translated into Arabic, where it was studied by Islamic scholars.
